alex: heads-up — seeing a regression when we co-host small-chat-7B + embedder on a single A100. p99 latency up ~15% vs last week after the kernel selection tweak. :confused:

alex: profiler snippet from canary run (short):
```
selected_kernel=matmul_fused_v2
seq_len=1024 batch=1
kv_cache_hits=0.62 kv_cache_misses=0.38
alloc_slow_path_ms=12.4 free_frag_ms=4.1
workspace_zero_ms=3.6 copy_into_workspace_ms=7.8
end_to_end_p99_ms=243 -> 280
```

maria: oh interesting — did the runtime switch the default kernel heuristics for med-size mats? last patch replaced fallback order so `v2` can be picked earlier. could be more workspace churn. @alex can you paste the exact run command? :eyes:

alex: repro command is tiny: `./bench --model small-chat-7b --cohost embedder-1 --seq 1024 --batch 1 --profile`
I also dumped allocator traces: `alloc slab_alloc(size=...) -> slow_path` spikes when we hit cross-model allocation boundary.

chen: my hunch: when single GPU hosts multiple models their KV residency pattern differs — warm KV for chat, cold for embedder. Kernel v2 seems to allocate a larger temporary workspace and doesn't reuse zeroed buffers efficiently, so we allocate + free between model boundaries. idea: partial-kv prefetch + async prewarm of workspace memory for incoming model slices.

chen: pseudo: 
```
on_route_request(model):
  if !kv_resident(model) and model.size < prefetch_thresh:
    async_prefetch_kv_layers(model, top_n=4)
  prewarm_workspace(model.id, hint=last_kernel)
```

priya: also check `workspace_bytes` sizing change in the kernel selector — recently added `max(estimated, 128MB)` to avoid tiny allocations. that saves branching for big mats but hurts co-residency. if we can reuse per-stream buffers with `reuse_buffers=true` we might avoid the slow_path. did you test with buffer reuse toggled?

alex: I tried `reuse_buffers=true` earlier — reduced alloc slow_path but p99 still high. looks like copy_into_workspace spikes when switching kernel because v2 writes into a different layout.

sam: two practical mitigations we tried in past experiments: soft-evict + buffer aliasing. mark cold model KV as reclaimable (soft-evict metadata) instead of immediate free, keep buffers pinned but marked "cold" so kernel can avoid zeroing when reusing. also add a small LRU pool per-GPU for cross-model temp buffers. results from a local sim: swap_rate 0.78 -> 0.12 and p99 down ~9% with aliasing + prewarm.

sam: (high level) steps:
1) on unload mark kv as soft-evict (retain memory but unmap from model table)
2) when a new model needs workspace, try rebind from soft pool instead of fresh alloc
3) prefetch minimal top-layers of KV async to amortize latency

alex: that lines up with my traces. can we try a small patch that disables kernel v2 for co-hosted pods (or forces workspace layout compat) and enable the soft-evict pool? quick canary to validate.

maria: +1 on a targeted canary. if we gate by `cohost_count > 1` we can avoid affecting single-model perf. add perf counters: `workspace_reuse_hits`, `soft_evicted_bytes`, `kv_prefetch_latency_ms` so we can quantify.

infra-bot: canary deploy started: infra/canary/soft-evict-pool at commit 6a9f2d — routing 5% traffic to canary.

alex: thanks — I'll attach profiler outputs once canary warms. will also run microbench matrix across kernels (v1/v2/v3), reuse_buffers T/F, prefetch top_n 0/2/4. posting results here in ~30m. :thumbsup:
